Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR CANNED APRICOT 0.
0.1 This

FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 26 February 1981, after the draft finalized by the Fruits and Vegetables Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Canned apricot is the product prepared from mature apricots of suitable varieties. The apricots are split into halves, destoned and packed They are processed in an appropriate manner before in suitable syrup. and after being sealed in a container so as to prevent spoilage. 0.3 Canned apricot is a product of commercial importance in India. There is ample scope for the development of the external as well as internal trade. It is, however, necessary to ensure the quality of the product, In order to if the demand is to be maintained and further developed. ensure proper quality, it is necessary to have a strict quality control based on specifications. It was, therefore, found necessary to formulate an Indian Standard Specification for this product. 0.4 In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and However, this standard is subject to the the Fruit Products Order, 1955. restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance The number of significant places retained in the with IS : 2-1960*. rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements for apricot, L ( Syn. Armeniaca vulgaris Lamk ) canned in syrup.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised).

4. GRADES

5. REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Hygienic Requirements -The material shall be prepared and handled under strict hygienic conditions by persons free from contagious and infectious diseases and only in premises maintained in thoroughly clean and hygienic conditions and having adequate and safe water supply duly approved and licensed by the public health authorities concerned. All workers shall use clean, white and washed clothing ( see IS : 65421972 * ). Necessary precautions shall be taken to prevent incidental contamination of the product from soiled equipment or from personnel suffering from injuries.

5.1.1 All equipment coming in contact with raw materials or products in the course of manufacture shall be kept clean. An ample supply of steam and water, hose, brushes and other equipment necessary for proper cleaning of machinery and equipment shall be available. The equipment may be sterilized by immersion in, or swabbing with hypochlorite or other suitable chlorine solution. 5.2 General - The varieties specially suited to canning, shall be used ( see 3.1 ). The apricot selected for canning shall be of good quality, proper stage of maturity and shall have the characteristic colour, tlavour and texture. The fruit canned shall be in sound condition, free from blemishes and damage by insects or disease, discolouration and disintegration. 5.3 Freedom from Artificial Colouring Matter, Flavour and Synthetic Sweetening Agents - The material shall be free from artificial colouring matter and flavouring and synthetic sweetening agents. 5.4 Requirements for Covering Syrup - The covering syrup shall be clear. It shall be made from nutritive sweetness like sucrose, dextrose or glucose. The citric acid and/or ascorbic acid may be added to the covering syrup.
*Code for hygienic conditions for fruit and vegetable canning units. 5

1s : 9789 - 1981
5.5 Requirements for the Finished Product - The can on opening shall display the following characteristics: contents of the

a)

Grade 1 - The canned apricot shall possess a good, characteristic and practically uniform colour; shall be practically uniform in size; free from defects and be intact; shall possess a tender and firm texture and normal characteristic flavour and shall secure not less than 85 points. Grade 2 - The canned apricot shall possess a good and reasonably uniform colour; shall be reasonably uniform in size; free from defects and be intact; shall possess a reasonably tender and firm texture and normal flavour and shall score not less than 70 points.

b)

NOTIZ- Scoring shall be done according to the method prescribed in Appendix A and the maximum and minimum number of points to be scored by different factors shall be as given in Table 1. 5.5.1 a)

Colour
Gkade I - The units shall possess a good practically uniform colour characteristic of well matured fruit; practically free from any discolouration due to over ripeness, oxidation, handling, processing or any other cause. The colour of the fruit shall be orange to golden yellow depending on the variety. Grade 2 - The unit shall possess a good reasonably uniform colour, which means that colour shall be orange to golden yellow in shades of the typical colour; and the fruit shall be reasonably free from discolouration due to oxidation, handling, processing or any other cause. Texture and Uniformity of Size

b)

5.5.2

apricots shall possess proper texture, a) Grade 1 - The canned which means that the units are of proper thickness, fleshy, full of juice and not fibrous and have a soft bite. They shall be neatly cut. The units in any one can shall be of uniform size. 6

Taste andjavour Grade 1 - The canned apricots shall possess pleasant aroma and flavour characteristic of the variety apricot canned. The taste shall be sweet and characteristic of the variety. The units shall be devoid of any objectionable or off taste, smell or odour indicative of unripe ( sour and fibrous ) fruit.

b) Grade 2 - The canned apricots shall possess pleasant aroma and flavour characteristic of the variety of apricot canned. The taste shall be sweet and characteristic of the variety. The units shall be devoid of any objectionable or off-taste, smell or odour indicative of unripe ( sour and fibrous ) friflit. 5.5.4

Absence of defects

free from a) Grade 1 - The canned apricots shall be practically defects and crushed or broken units. The blemished units shall not be more than 5 percent of drained mass or one unit by count and no unit shall be trimmed to the extent that the normal shape of the unit is destroyed. The covering syrup shall be practically clear, free from cloudiness, blackening or thickening and be practically free from fruit pulp. b) shall be reasonably free from Grade 2 - The canned apricots defects and crushed or broken units. The blemished units shall not be more than 10 percent of drained mass or two units by count and no unit shall be trimmed to the extent that the normal shape of the units is destroyed. In case the units are disintegrated, the disintegrated portion shall not be more than 5 percent of the drained mass. The covering syrup shall be reasonably clear, free from cloudiness, blackening or thickening and reasonably free from fruit pulp. shall also conform to the requirements prescribed

A-2. PROCEDURE A-2.1 Panel of Judges - Scoring of product shall be done by a panel of three to five judges. All the judges constituting a panel shall be conversant The cans shall be with the factors governing the quality of the product. opened and the contents poured separately into white porcelain bowls. Each judge shall independently examine the contents from each of the cans and assign scores for different characteristics.
A-2.1.1 The judges shall consider and uniformity the following characteristics:

Colour, texture of defects.

of size, taste and flavour and absence

A-2.2 System of Scoring - The variations within each factor are so described that the scores may be ascertained for each factor and expressed numerically. The relative importance of each factor has been expressed Each judge shall give a score for the indinumerically on a scale of 100. vidual factors, by the method described in Table 3 and record his observations in the Score Sheet for Individual Judge. A-2.2.1 The scores as number of points given on the Score Sheet by the judges for the contents of each can for the four factors shall be recorded in a tabular form in the Score Card and the average score calculated for each factor with overall average for each can entered in the appropriate columns of the score card after complying with the conditions given in A-2.3.1 and A-2.3.2.

is : 9789 - 1981 A-2.3 Ascertaining the Grade

A-2.3.1 Agreement Among Judges - To ascertain the consistency of judgement among the judges, the total score assigned by each of them for the contents of the same can shall be calculated by adding up the score for the various individual characteristics. If the difference between the maximum and the minimum of the total score so obtained does not exceed ( K + 5 ), where K is the number of judges, the scoring shall be deemed as consistent for the can under consideration. If the difference exceeds ( K + 5 ), the most outlying score, that is, the one which is farthest from its immediate neighbour ( the scores being arranged in one order ), shall be discarded and the consistency among the remaining judges shall be examined. A-2.3.2 When the consistency is thus established ( A-2.3.1), the overall average scores given by the judges, whose scoring has been found to be consistent, shall be calculated for each can. The average score for each of the individual characteristics shall also be calculated by taking into account the corresponding scores as given by the same judges for the contents of the same can. AMENDMENT NO. 1 MAY 1996 TO IS 9789 : 1981 SPECIFICATION FOR CANNED APRICOT ( Page 3, Foreword, clause 0.4 ) - Insextthe following new clause after 0.4
and renumber the subsequent clause: `0.5 A scheme for labclling environment friendly products known as ECO-Mark has been introduced at the instance of the Ministry of Environment and Fotests (MEF), Government of India. The ECO-Mark shall be administered by the Buteau of Indian Standards (BIS) under the BZSAct, 1986 as per the Resolution No. 71 dated 20 February 1991 and Resolution No. 425 dated 28 October 1992 published in the Gazette of the Government of India. For a product to be eligible for marking with the EC0 Mark it shall also carry the Standard Mark of BIS for quality besides meeting additional environment friendly (EF) requirements. The environment friendly requirements for canned apricot are, therefore, included through Amendment No. 1 to this standard. This `amendment is based on the Gazette Notification No. 624 (E) dated 6 September 1995 for Labelling Beverages, Infant Foods, Processed Fruits and Vegetable Products as environment friendly, published in the Gazette of the Government of India.' ( Page 7, clause 555 ) - Insert the following new matter after 5.5.!3: "5.6 Additional Requirements for ECO-Mark 5.6.1 Gepzral Requirements 5.6.1.1 The product shall conform to the requirements prescribed under 5.1 to 55.5. 5.6.1.2 The manufacturer shall produce the consent clearance as per the provisions of Water (PCP) Act, 1974, Water (PCP) Cess Act, 1977 and Air (PCP) Act, 1981 along with the authorization if required under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the Rules made thereunder to the Bureau of Indian Standards while applying for the ECO-Mark and the product shall also be in accordance with the Prevention of FoodAdulteration Act, 1954 and the Rules made thereunder. Additionally, FPO 1955 (Fruit Product Order) framed under Essential Comnudities Act, 1955, Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1977 requirements wherever applicable has to be complied with. 1
